q: can I give Motrin to my 8 month old for fever
text: Yes, ibuprofen (Motrin) can be given to a child over 6 months old — it should not be used in children younger than 6 months, according to MedlinePlus [6]. It helps reduce fever, and is usually given every 6 to 8 hours [6]. Know how much your child weighs before giving it [6]. The dose depends on the child's weight; check the packaging or leaflet to make sure the medicine is suitable for your child, or speak to a pharmacist or doctor if you're not sure [3]. You can also give paracetamol instead, but do not alternate ibuprofen and paracetamol unless a doctor or nurse tells you to [2]. Keep breastfeeding as normal and watch for signs of dehydration [3]. Get medical advice if you're worried, or if the medicine is not helping [3].

q: my son threw up twice this morning, what should I give him to drink
text:
For vomiting, the goal is to replace the fluids and electrolytes your son has lost. Oral rehydration solutions are made for children and you can buy them without a prescription, according to MedlinePlus [1]. Give small sips of rehydration solution regularly to replace lost fluids [6]. If he is on formula or solid foods, you can also give small sips of extra water [6]. Do not give young children fruit juice or fizzy drinks — they can make vomiting worse [6]. Do not make formula weaker [6]. Keep giving his usual diet in small amounts [6].

q: how do I know if my child is getting dehydrated from vomiting
text:
Dehydration happens when the body loses more fluid than it takes in, and vomiting is one of the common causes [1]. The main risk of vomiting is dehydration, so the priority is keeping fluids going in [3].

When your child vomits, wait 20 minutes, then give oral rehydration solution — 2 to 5 ml every 5 minutes for an hour, according to the SEUP [5]. Watch how well they take it; if fluids go down well, you can slowly increase how often you offer them [5]. Don't use homemade solutions like lemonade, or commercial soft drinks [5]. Oral rehydration fluids you can buy over the counter are the most helpful for mild dehydration, and sports drinks without caffeine or alcohol can help a little, though they don't replace important nutrients and minerals, according to the CDC [2].

Get medical care if you think your child is severely dehydrated — that can need fluids through a vein in hospital [2]. Also check with your paediatrician if your child seems floppy or listless, vomits many times, or won't take fluids [3].

text:
A cough that is worse at night is one of the main signs of asthma in children, according to MedlinePlus [6]. Asthma symptoms usually come and go, and may be worse at night and early in the morning [4].

If your child has asthma, keep using their inhaler as usual, and see your doctor if treatments are not helping, if they need their inhaler more often, or if you need advice about using it [4]. See your doctor if your child has asthma symptoms, or if symptoms are not improving, are stopping them doing their usual activities, or are waking them up at night [4].

Get medical help right away if there is severe coughing, serious breathing problems, or if they turn very pale or blue in the face, lips or fingernails [6].

q: my son has been coughing for a week after a cold
text:
A cough that lingers after a cold is common: cold symptoms can last for 10 to 14 days, according to MedlinePlus [6]. Keep offering fluids and let your son rest; there is no medicine that shortens a cold.

If the cough changes — bouts of coughing that last for a few minutes and are worse at night, a "whoop" sound when gasping between coughs, thick mucus that makes him vomit, or difficulty breathing after a coughing bout — that is not a simple cold, and he should be seen, according to the NHS [4]. In babies under 3 months, pauses in breathing or turning blue or grey need medical care right away [4].

q: he has a cough but no fever and is eating normally
text:
A cough without a fever, with a child eating normally, is not one of the situations the guidance covers as a fever problem — fever is the body's natural response to fighting infections like coughs and colds, according to the NHS [1].

If a fever does appear, the AEPap says to first check the temperature with a thermometer, in the armpit, and if there are no warning signs start with physical measures: remove extra clothing, offer fluids, reduce physical activity and a lukewarm bath if the child is comfortable [4]. Antitérmicos are used when the temperature is above 38-38.5°C (101.3 °F) in the armpit or when the fever causes discomfort [6]. Paracetamol can be given every 4-6 hours, no more than five doses a day, and ibuprofen every 6-8 hours; the dose is calculated by weight, not age [6].

Get help if your child has other signs of illness such as a rash alongside a high temperature, has a high temperature lasting 5 days or more, does not want to eat or is not their usual self and you are worried, or is dehydrated, according to the NHS [1].

q: my daughter has red spots all over her stomach and they appeared today
text:
Red spots that appear suddenly and itch a lot are often hives, which in childhood are mostly caused by an infection rather than an allergy, according to the SEUP [3]. The spots are raised, red patches that move around — appearing in one area as they fade from another — and can come with swelling of the hands, feet, elbows or face [3].

Hives can usually be treated at home [5]. Keep your daughter comfortable, and speak to a pharmacist about antihistamine medicine to help with itching [1]. Bathing in cool water and patting the skin dry without rubbing can help, as can loose clothes [1]. Paracetamol can help with any pain or discomfort [1].

Call your local emergency number if there is swelling around her mouth or she is struggling to breathe [5].

q: these spots dont seem to bother her but there are more every morning
text:
Many things can cause a rash in babies and children, according to the NHS [3]. Small, firm, raised spots could be molluscum contagiosum, and these can be the same colour as the surrounding skin, darker, or pink; you can usually treat molluscum contagiosum at home [6]. Spots on the nappy area can appear red or brown, and may be harder to see on brown and black skin [2].

Call your local emergency number or go to the emergency department now if your child is unwell with a rash and has any of these symptoms: a stiff neck; is bothered by light; seems confused, agitated or is not responding like they usually do; difficulty breathing (you may notice grunting noises or their tummy sucking under their ribs), breathlessness, or breathing very fast; their skin, lips or tongue look pale, blue, grey or blotchy; sudden swelling of their lips, mouth, throat or tongue; their throat feels tight or they are struggling to swallow; or the rash looks like small bruises or bleeding under the skin and does not fade when you press a glass against it [3]. On brown and black skin, it may be easier to see the rash or colour changes on the soles of the feet, palms, lips, tongue and inside the eyelids [3].

q: my 6 year old fell from the bed and hit the back of his head
text:
Most head injuries are not serious, and most children recover quickly, according to the SEUP [2][6]. The usual symptoms are headache, confusion, brief memory loss, dizziness, nausea, vomiting and drowsiness [1].

Let him rest, physically and mentally, for 24 to 48 hours depending on how hard the knock was — no sport and no screens (tablets, video games, smartphones) during that time, then a gradual return to normal activity [4]. He can sleep, but after a more significant knock it is worth waking him every 4 hours [6]. He can eat and drink as usual, according to his appetite [6]. If he has a headache, you can give ibuprofen or paracetamol in the dose your doctor indicates [6].

Go to the emergency department if he has any of the symptoms above, or any behaviour that worries you — also if the fall was from more than one metre [5].

q: what foods should I start with for a baby who just turned 6 months
text: Start with single vegetables and fruits, according to the NHS. Try mashed or soft, cooked sticks of parsnip, broccoli, potato, yam, sweet potato, carrot, apple or pear [5]. Include vegetables that are not sweet, such as broccoli, cauliflower and spinach, to help your baby get used to a range of flavours [5]. Make sure any cooked food has cooled right down before offering it [5]. Foods containing allergens, such as peanuts, hens' eggs, gluten and fish, can be introduced from around 6 months, one at a time and in small amounts so you can spot any reaction [5]. Full-fat dairy products such as pasteurised cheese and plain yoghurt can be given from around 6 months; choose ones with no added sugar [5]. Babies do not need salt or sugar added to their food or cooking water [5]. At first, how much your baby eats matters less than getting them used to eating — they still get most of their energy and nutrients from breast milk or first infant formula [1].

q: my daughter is 13 months and still mostly drinks formula
text:
Once your child is 12 months old, formula milks are not needed, according to the NHS [2]. This includes first infant formula, follow-on formula, growing-up milks and other toddler milks [2]. Your baby can now drink pasteurised whole or semi-skimmed cows' milk [2]. Choose full-fat dairy products such as cheese, yoghurt and fromage frais, as children under 2 years old need the vitamins and extra energy found in them [2].

From 12 months, your child will be eating 3 meals a day containing a variety of different foods, including starchy food such as potatoes, bread and rice; fruit and vegetables; milk or dairy products; and protein from animal sources (meat, fish and eggs) or vegetable sources (dhal, beans, chickpeas and lentils) [2]. Your child may also need 2 healthy snacks in between meals [2]. Go for things like fresh fruits such as slices of apple and banana, or small pieces of soft, ripe, peeled pear or peach; cooked or raw vegetables such as broccoli florets, carrot sticks or cucumber sticks; pasteurised plain, unsweetened, full-fat yoghurt; sticks of cheese (choose a lower salt option); toast, pitta or chapatti fingers; and unsalted and unsweetened rice or corn cakes [2].

The World Health Organization recommends that all babies are breastfed for up to 2 years or longer [2]. You can keep breastfeeding for as long as it suits you both, but your child will need less breast milk to make room for more foods [2]. You can give your child unsweetened, calcium-fortified milk alternatives, such as soya, oat or almond drinks, from the age of 1 as their main drink as part of a healthy, balanced diet [2]. A dietitian can give you advice on milk alternatives to make sure your child is getting the nutrients they need [2]. Children under 5 years old should not be given rice drinks because of the levels of arsenic in these products [2].

q: how often should a newborn poop
text: How often a newborn poops varies from baby to baby — the rhythm and consistency of stools differs from one person to another, according to the SEUP [3]. It is not essential that a baby has a bowel movement every day [3]. What matters more is whether the stools become hard: constipation is an excessive increase in the hardness of the stool, with discomfort or incomplete emptying, and it may come with fewer bowel movements [6]. For a baby under 6 months, keep feeding as usual with breast milk or formula [3]. Constipation should be checked by your paediatrician unless it comes with: significant abdominal pain, being very down and complaining a lot, blood in the stool, or vomiting many times and not tolerating solids or liquids [3]. Never give laxatives or enemas without consulting your paediatrician [3].

q: my 4 year old wakes up coughing only when he lies down
text:
A cough that comes on mainly when your child lies down can be a sign of asthma, which often causes coughing at night or early in the morning, according to MedlinePlus [3]. Asthma symptoms usually come and go and may be worse at night and early in the morning, according to the NHS [4].

Keep the air moist — water can help ease a cough, whether your child drinks it or you add it to the air with a steamy shower or vaporizer [1]. Do not give cough medicine: children under four should not have it, and for children over four you should use caution and read labels carefully [1].

See your doctor if your child has asthma symptoms, or if symptoms are waking them up at night [4]. Get medical help right away if there is severe coughing, serious breathing problems, or your child turns very pale or blue in the face, lips or fingernails [3].

On steam, guidelines differ. The CDC suggests sitting with a young child in a bathroom with steam from a running shower to ease a cough. The NHS advises against it: with croup, do not put your child in a steamy room or get them to inhale steam, and do not let children breathe in steam from a bowl of hot water, because of the risk of scalding.

q: my son has asthma and is using albuterol more than usual
text: Using a reliever inhaler more often can mean your child's asthma is not as well controlled as it should be, according to the NHS [2]. Keep using the inhaler as your child's plan says, and make sure it is used correctly — a doctor, nurse or pharmacist can show you how [3]. If your child is having an asthma attack, sit them up straight to help their breathing and try to stay calm [4]. With a blue reliever inhaler, give 1 puff every 30 to 60 seconds until they feel better, up to a maximum of 10 puffs, shaking the inhaler between each puff and using a spacer if you have one [4]. With an AIR or MART inhaler, give 1 puff every 1 to 3 minutes, up to a maximum of 6 puffs [4]. If your child's personal asthma action plan has a different maximum dose, follow that plan [4]. Get help now if your child starts to feel worse at any time, does not feel better after the maximum dose of reliever inhaler, or does not have an inhaler [4]. If symptoms are no better after 10 minutes and help has not arrived, use the inhaler again, up to the same maximum dose [4]. After an attack, even if your child feels better, see your doctor within 2 days to discuss treatment and help prevent another attack [4]. See your doctor if your child needs their inhaler more often, treatments are not helping, or symptoms are stopping them doing usual activities or waking them at night [2].

q: she is making a strange noise when she breathes but is still smiling
text:
A strange noise when breathing can be a sign of croup, which is an inflammation of the vocal cords and windpipe that causes noisy breathing, a dry barking cough and a hoarse voice, according to MedlinePlus [3]. It often starts like a cold, and symptoms usually get worse at night and last three to five days [3]. Most viral cases are mild and can be treated at home [3].

Keep the child calm and comfortable, and offer fluids often. Croup is more common in children between six months and three years, and more frequent in autumn and winter [3].

If you are worried about your child's breathing, call your doctor straight away, according to MedlinePlus [3]. Croup can rarely become severe and interfere with breathing [3].

q: my 6 year old says his chest hurts when he takes a deep breath
text:
Chest pain when breathing deeply can be a sign of asthma, according to the WHO. Asthma symptoms include chest tightness that makes it hard to breathe deeply, and they are often worse at night or during exercise [1]. Symptoms can also be caused by other conditions, so anyone with symptoms should talk to a healthcare provider [1].

Watch your child's general state at home, and look for difficulty breathing — ribs showing or the chest sinking in, fast breathing, getting tired when walking or running — or chest pain when breathing, according to the SEUP [2]. Go to the emergency department if their general state gets worse, if they are listless, sleepy or very irritable, or if difficulty breathing appears [2]. Chest pain or pain in the side when breathing is also a reason to go, so complications can be ruled out [5].

q: my baby had a seizure last year and has a fever today
text:
A febrile seizure can happen when a child has a high temperature, and it is not usually serious, according to the NHS [3]. A high temperature is 38C (100.4 °F) or more, and it usually returns to normal within 1 to 4 days [1].

A sore throat that hurts when swallowing is very common and usually nothing to worry about — it normally gets better by itself within a week, according to the NHS [5]. It is usually caused by a virus, like a cold or flu [4].

To help soothe it: drink plenty of water, eat cool or soft foods, suck ice cubes, ice lollies or hard sweets, rest, and avoid smoking or smoky places [5]. She can gargle with warm salty water — half a teaspoon of salt in a glass of warm water, then spit it out, not swallow it [5].

Antibiotics are not normally needed, because they will not usually relieve symptoms or speed up recovery [7]. Get help if her sore throat does not improve after a week, or if she has a lump in her mouth or neck or a mouth ulcer lasting more than 3 weeks [7]. Ask for urgent advice now if you are worried, if she has a very high temperature or feels hot, cold or shivery, or if she has signs of dehydration such as peeing less than usual or dark, strong-smelling pee [7]. q: my child keeps scratching red patches on his arms
text:
Itchy red patches on the arms are common in children and are often a sign of eczema, a skin condition that most often starts in babies and young children, according to the NHS [1]. Scratching can make the skin turn red and swell and itch even more [2].

Keep nails short, and put anti-scratch mittens on babies to limit damage from scratching [5]. Apply moisturising treatments (emollients) to the skin as often as possible, at least twice a day, and keep moisturising even if the eczema improves [5]. Wash with an emollient instead of soap, avoid things that make it worse such as soap, washing detergent, some fabrics or pets, and keep your child cool, because being hot makes eczema more itchy [5].

See your doctor if your child has symptoms of atopic eczema, or if treatments are not helping [4]. Ask for an urgent appointment if the skin is blistered, crusty, leaking fluid or has spots filled with pus; if it is painful, swollen or feels warm; if it suddenly gets worse or gets bigger; or if your child has a high temperature or feels generally unwell [4].

q: my daughter has mosquito bites all over her legs, what can I put

Most insect bites are harmless, though they sometimes cause discomfort, and mosquito bites usually itch [6]. The bite should get better in a few days [1].

Put an ice pack wrapped in a cloth, or a clean cloth soaked in cold water, on the bites for at least 20 minutes, and keep the area raised if it's swollen [1]. text:
अगर बच्चा 3 महीने से छोटा है, तो बुखार में उसी दिन डॉक्टर को दिखाना ज़रूरी है।

बुखार के साथ लाल दाने कई चीज़ों से हो सकते हैं। हैंड, फुट एंड माउथ डिज़ीज़ में पहले गले में दर्द, तेज़ बुखार और खाने का मन न करना होता है, और कुछ दिन बाद मुँह में छाले तथा हाथ-पैरों पर, कभी-कभी ग्रोइन और नितंबों पर, उभरे हुए लाल दाने निकल आते हैं; ये लक्षण आमतौर पर हल्के होते हैं, ऐसा NHS कहता है [3]। यह बीमारी आमतौर पर 7 से 10 दिन में खुद ठीक हो जाती है और इसे ठीक करने की कोई दवा नहीं है [1]। लक्षणों में मदद के लिए ठंडे तरल पदार्थ पिलाएँ ताकि मुँह को आराम मिले और पानी की कमी न हो, पर खट्टे पेय जैसे फलों का रस न दें; दही जैसा नरम खाना दें और गरम, नमकीन व मसालेदार खाना न दें [1]। दर्द के लिए पैरासिटामोल या आइबुप्रोफेन दी जा सकती है, पर खुराक बच्चे की उम्र और वज़न पर निर्भर करती है [1]। मुँह के छालों के लिए फार्मासिस्ट से जेल, स्प्रे या माउथवॉश के बारे में पूछें; वे बता देंगे कि बच्चों के लिए कौन-से ठीक हैं [1]।

अगर दाने चेहरे या गर्दन पर निकलकर पूरे शरीर पर फैल रहे हैं, तो यह खसरा हो सकता है — ऐसे में डॉक्टर से बात करें [1]।

बच्चे की उम्र कितनी है? उम्र जानकर मैं जवाब और सटीक कर सकता हूँ।
sources: [1] NHS — "Rashes in babies and children" (2024), section "How to treat hand, foot and mou
[3] NHS — "Rashes in babies and children" (2024), section "Symptoms of hand, foot and mout

q: मेरा 6 महीने का बच्चा दूध कम पी रहा है और पेशाब भी कम कर रहा है
banner: 🚨 इन लक्षणों के साथ बच्चे को आज ही इमरजेंसी में दिखाना चाहिए, देर न करें। | कारण: पानी की कमी के लक्षण: आँखें धँसी, कम पेशाब, सूखा मुँह, लगातार उल्टी या 24 घंटे से ज़्यादा दस्त
text:
सबसे पहले, ऊपर की चेतावनी में जो लिखा है वह कीजिए।

मेडलाइनप्लस के अनुसार, पेशाब का कम आना या पेशाब का गाढ़ा होना और बदबू आना इस बात का संकेत हो सकता है कि बच्चा पर्याप्त तरल नहीं पी रहा है [3]। एनएचएस के अनुसार, बच्चे को पर्याप्त तरल, खासकर पानी, पिलाएँ ताकि वह दिन में नियमित रूप से पेशाब करे और प्यासा न लगे [4]। एसईयूपी के अनुसार, मुँह से पुनर्जलीकरण घोल (ओआरएस) थोड़ी-थोड़ी मात्रा में बार-बार दें, और घर के बने घोल या कोल्ड ड्रिंक्स इस्तेमाल न करें [1]। स्तनपान सामान्य रूप से, और अगर बच्चा माँगे तो उससे भी अधिक बार जारी रखें [8]। दस्त या उल्टी की दवा बिना बाल रोग विशेषज्ञ से पूछे न दें [1]।
sources: [1] SEUP — "Gastroenteritis aguda. Información para padres" (2025), section "Ofrecer en pe
[3] NHS — "Urinary tract infections (UTIs)" (2025), section "Urinary tract infections (UTI
[4] NHS — "Urinary tract infections (UTIs)" (2025), section "How to prevent urinary tract

q: मेरी बेटी बिस्तर से गिर गई और उसके बाद एक बार उल्टी हुई
banner: 🚨 इन लक्षणों के साथ बच्चे को आज ही इमरजेंसी में दिखाना चाहिए, देर न करें। | कारण: सिर पर चोट के बाद उल्टी
text:
सबसे पहले, ऊपर की चेतावनी में जो लिखा है वह कीजिए।

सिर की चोट के बाद उल्टी होना एक ऐसा लक्षण है जिस पर घर पर नज़र रखनी चाहिए, और SEUP के मुताबिक बार-बार उल्टी होना मतलब हालत बिगड़ने का संकेत हो सकता है [1]। चोट के बाद 24 से 48 घंटे तक शारीरिक और मानसिक आराम ज़रूरी है — इस दौरान खेल-कूद और मोबाइल, टैबलेट या वीडियो गेम जैसी चीज़ें नहीं [1]। इसके बाद धीरे-धीरे सामान्य गतिविधियों में लौटना चाहिए [1]।

घर पर इन बातों पर ध्यान दें: तेज़ या बढ़ता हुआ सिरदर्द जो आम दवा (पैरासिटामोल या इबुप्रोफेन) से ठीक न हो, बार-बार उल्टी, भ्रम या दिशा-भूलना — बहुत छोटे बच्चों में चिड़चिड़ापन या जगाने में मुश्किल, व्यवहार में बदलाव, बोलने या चलने में दिक्कत, और नाक या कान से खून या साफ़ तरल निकलना [1]।
sources: [1] SEUP — "Traumatismo craneal. Información para padres" (2025), section "¿CUÁNDO PUEDE V

q: बच्चे को कब्ज है और पॉटी करते समय बहुत रोता है
text:
कब्ज़ में पॉटी करते समय बच्चे का रोना आम बात है — रोने के सामान्य कारणों में कब्ज़ भी शामिल है, ऐसा NHS कहता है [2]।

अभी के लिए: बच्चे को आराम पहुँचाने की कोशिश करें और रोना शांत होने का इंतज़ार करें [1]। अगर पता न चले कि परेशानी क्या है, तो अपने डॉक्टर से बात करें या स्वास्थ्य कर्मी से पूछें [2]।

डॉक्टर से संपर्क करें अगर बच्चा लगातार रो रहा है और आप उसे चुप नहीं करा पा रहे, या उसका रोना उसके सामान्य रोने जैसा नहीं लग रहा, या उसमें बीमारी के संकेत हैं जैसे तेज़ बुखार या दूध पीने में दिलचस्पी न हो [4]। तुरंत मदद लें अगर बच्चे को दौरा पड़े, त्वचा-होंठ-जीभ नीले, स्लेटी, पीले या धब्बेदार दिखें, वह बेजान या सुस्त हो या आसानी से न जागे, साँस लेने में तकलीफ़ हो, बहुत ज़्यादा उल्टी हो, तापमान बहुत ज़्यादा या बहुत कम हो, दबाने पर न मिटने वाले दाने हों, या पिछले 8 घंटे में पेशाब की नैप्पी गीली न हुई हो [4]। अपनी अंतर्ज्ञान पर भरोसा करें [4]।

q: मेरे बच्चे के हाथ पैर ठंडे हैं लेकिन शरीर गर्म है
text:
जब बुखार चढ़ रहा होता है तो बच्चे का ठंड लगना, कंपकंपी आना और हाथ-पैरों का ठंडा होना सामान्य है — त्वचा पर जाल जैसा धब्बेदार रूप भी दिख सकता है, खासकर हाथों और पैरों पर। बुखार उतरते समय बच्चा पसीना-पसीना हो जाएगा, लाल हो जाएगा और उसे गर्मी लगेगी, ऐसा SEUP कहता है [1]।

बुखार आमतौर पर 2 से 4 दिन रहता है, हालांकि कुछ दिन ज़्यादा भी रह सकता है और इससे ज़्यादा गंभीरता नहीं जुड़ती। दवा से तापमान कम होता है, पर हमेशा पूरी तरह नहीं उतरता — खासकर अगर बुखार बहुत तेज़ हो; इसलिए दवा के बाद भी बुखार बना रहना आम है और इसका मतलब ज़्यादा गंभीर होना नहीं है [2]। बुखार शरीर की रक्षा का तरीका है, अपने आप में गंभीरता की निशानी नहीं [5]। बुखार में पानी की कमी से बचने के लिए पर्याप्त तरल देना ज़रूरी है [4]।

घर पर बच्चे की सामान्य हालत और रंग पर नज़र रखें, और त्वचा पर ऐसे लाल धब्बे दिखें जो दबाने पर गायब न हों तो ध्यान दें [2]। आपातकालीन सेवा में तुरंत जाएं अगर बच्चा सुस्त, कम प्रतिक्रिया देने वाला या बहुत चिड़चिड़ा हो; सांस लेने में तकलीफ हो; त्वचा पर दबाने से न मिटने वाले धब्बे हों; मुंह से ठोस या तरल कुछ भी न ले पा रहा हो; या बच्चा 2 महीने से छोटा हो या प्रतिरक्षा-दबाव वाला हो, ऐसा SEUP कहता है [7]।
sources: [1] SEUP — "Fiebre. Información para padres" (2025), section "¿CUÁLES SON LOS SÍNTOMAS?",
[2] SEUP — "Fiebre. Información para padres" (2025), section "¿CUÁL ES LA EVOLUCIÓN ESPERA
[4] MedlinePlus — "Fiebre", p. 1 — https://medlineplus.gov/spanish/fever.html

q: मेरा बच्चा बहुत सुस्त है और ठीक से जाग नहीं रहा
banner: 🚨 अभी 112 पर कॉल करें या तुरंत इमरजेंसी ले जाएँ। | कारण: जवाब नहीं दे रहा; बहुत ज़्यादा सुस्ती या चिड़चिड़ापन
text:
बच्चे का सुस्त हो जाना और ज़्यादा देर जागते न रहना निमोनिया की गंभीरता के संकेतों में गिना जाता है, विकासपीडिया के अनुसार [2]। ऐसे में तुरंत वैद्यकीय सहायता लेनी चाहिए [2]।

जब तक मदद मिले, बच्चे को अपने पास रखें और उसका खाना-पीना चालू रखने की कोशिश करें [2]। बुखार उतारने के लिए गुनगुने पानी में कपड़ा भिगोकर पूरा शरीर पोंछें, सिर्फ माथा नहीं [2]।

अस्पताल ले जाते समय इन बातों का ध्यान रखें: बुखार से दौरे पड़ना, बच्चे का खाने-पीने या स्तनपान को राजी न होना, साँस लेते समय पसलियों का अंदर खिंचना, सीने से कराहने या सींटी जैसी आवाज़ आना, और त्वचा, होंठ, नाखून या चेहरे पर नीली झलक दिखना — इनमें से कोई भी लक्षण दिखते ही तुरंत वैद्यकीय सहायता लेनी चाहिए [2]।
sources: [2] Vikaspedia — "बच्चों को होने वाली आम बीमारियॉं — स्रोत: भारत स्वास्थ्य" (2020), sectio

q: मेरे बच्चे ने आज बहुत कम पेशाब किया है
banner: 🚨 इन लक्षणों के साथ बच्चे को आज ही इमरजेंसी में दिखाना चाहिए, देर न करें। | कारण: पानी की कमी के लक्षण: आँखें धँसी, कम पेशाब, सूखा मुँह, लगातार उल्टी या 24 घंटे से ज़्यादा दस्त
text:
बहुत कम पेशाब आना निर्जलीकरण का संकेत हो सकता है, और प्यास बहुत लगना, बिना आँसू के रोना या आँखें धँसी दिखना भी इसी ओर इशारा करते हैं, SEUP के अनुसार [1]।

अब ओरल रीहाइड्रेशन सॉल्यूशन (ORS) थोड़ी-थोड़ी मात्रा में बार-बार दें — तैयार मिलने वाला घोल इस्तेमाल करें, घर के बने घोल या कोल्ड ड्रिंक न दें [1]। बच्चा जितना तरल खो रहा है, उतना ही पी सके, यह ध्यान रखें [1]। दस्त या उल्टी की दवा बिना बाल रोग विशेषज्ञ से पूछे न दें [1]। खाना बंद करने की ज़रूरत नहीं; सामान्य खाना थोड़ी-थोड़ी मात्रा में, बार-बार दें, और बच्चे की भूख का सम्मान करें [8]। चिकनी चीज़ें, मिठाई और जूस से बचें; दूध और स्तनपान सामान्य रूप से जारी रखें, माँगे तो और बार [8]। स्पोर्ट्स ड्रिंक न दें [8]।

डॉक्टर से तुरंत मिलें अगर बच्चा बहुत उल्टी करे, ठोस या तरल कुछ भी न रख पाए, बिना कुछ पिए भी उल्टी करे, या उल्टी हरी हो, उसमें खून हो या कॉफ़ी जैसी भूरी दिखे [8]।
sources: [1] SEUP — "Gastroenteritis aguda. Información para padres" (2025), section "Ofrecer en pe
[8] SEUP — "Gastroenteritis aguda. Información para padres" (2025), section "¿DEBEMOS OFRE

q: मेरी बेटी को तेज बुखार और बैंगनी जैसे दाग हो गए हैं
banner: 🚨 अभी 112 पर कॉल करें या तुरंत इमरजेंसी ले जाएँ। | कारण: दबाने पर न मिटने वाले दाने (सेप्सिस या मेनिन्जाइटिस का शक)
text:
अगर बच्चा 3 महीने से छोटा है, तो बुखार में उसी दिन डॉक्टर को दिखाना ज़रूरी है।

तेज़ बुखार बच्चों में बहुत आम है और आमतौर पर 1 से 4 दिनों में तापमान सामान्य हो जाता है, एनएचएस के अनुसार [3]। त्वचा पर ऐसे दाग जो दबाने पर भी न मिटें, तो तुरंत मदद लेनी चाहिए — एसईयूपी कहती है कि ऐसे दाग होने पर आपातकालीन सेवा में जाना चाहिए [1]।

जब तक मदद मिले: बच्चे को बहुत ज़्यादा कपड़ों या रज़ाई में न लपेटें, और उसे ठंडा करने के लिए कपड़े न उतारें या स्पंज न करें — तेज़ तापमान संक्रमण के खिलाफ शरीर की स्वाभाविक प्रतिक्रिया है, एनएचएस के अनुसार [2]। 16 साल से छोटे बच्चे को एस्पिरिन न दें, और डॉक्टर या नर्स के कहे बिना आइबुप्रोफेन और पैरासिटामोल बारी-बारी न दें [2]। दवा की मात्रा बच्चे की उम्र और वज़न पर निर्भर करती है, इसलिए वह डॉक्टर या दवा के पर्चे के अनुसार ही दें।

एसईयूपी के अनुसार, अगर बच्चा सुस्त या कम प्रतिक्रिया देने वाला या बहुत चिड़चिड़ा हो, सांस लेने में तकलीफ हो, दबाने पर न मिटने वाले दाग हों, मुँह से कुछ भी न ले पाए, या बच्चा 2 महीने से छोटा हो या प्रतिरक्षा कमज़ोर हो, तो आपातकालीन सेवा में जाएँ [1]।

q: mera baby raat ko bahut khans raha hai
text:
Raat mein khansi hona kai cheezon mein se ek lakshan ho sakta hai. MedlinePlus ke mutabik bachchon mein asthma ke lakshanon mein khansi shaamil hai, khaaskar raat ko ya subah jaldi [1]. SEUP ke mutabik asthma ke daure mein bachchon ko raat ko khansi, saans ki kami aur ghabrahat ho sakti hai [3].

Ghar par aaram karayein, khoob saara taraL peeyein, saaf humidifier ya thande bhaap wala vaporizer istemaal karein, aur saline naak ki boondein ya spray dein [6]. SEUP ke mutabik khansi ke syrup, mucolytics, corticoide ya respiratory physiotherapy faydemand nahi hain [2]. Kisi bhi dawa se pehle apne doctor se poochein [6].

Turant medical madad lein agar saans lene mein sakht dikkat ho, khansi lagataar ho, bolne mein dikkat ho, ya honton ke aas-paas neela rang dikhe [3].

q: mere bete ke pairon par lal dane hain aur khujli ho rahi hai
text: Chhote, ubhre hue lal dane jo khujli karte hain, aksar heat rash (prickly heat) hote hain — yeh takleef deta hai par aam taur par harmless hota hai aur kuch dinon mein khud theek ho jata hai, NHS ke mutabiq [6]. Sabse zaroori hai skin ko thanda rakhna taaki pasina aakar rash ko na chidhaye: dheele cotton kapde pehnao, halki rajai use karo, thande paani se nahi ya shower karao, aur dehydration se bachne ke liye khoob paani pilao [6]. Khujli ya chubhan shaant karne ke liye thandi cheez — geele kapde ya ice pack (towel mein lipti hui) — 20 minute tak lagao, aur khujlane ke bajaye rash ko thapthapao ya sehlayo; khushbudar shower gel ya cream mat lagao [6]. Agar saans lene mein dikkat ho ya munh ke aas-paas sujan ho to turant emergency help lein, NHS ke mutabiq [5].

Bed se girne ke baad ek baar ulti hona — SEUP ke mutabik, sar par chot lagne ke baad ulti aana ek aisa lakshan hai jise doctor ko dikhana chahiye [1]. Ghar par 24 se 48 ghante tak sharirik aur mansik aaram karein, khel-kood aur mobile, tablet ya video games bilkul na karein [1]. Aaram ke baad normal kaam dhire-dhire shuru karein [1].

q: mere bacche ko kabz hai aur potty karte waqt rota hai
text:
Mere bachche ko kabz hai aur potty karte waqt rota hai — yeh aam baat hai, kyunki constipation un kai kaaranon mein se ek hai jinki wajah se bachche rote hain, NHS ke mutabik [3].

Agar bachcha breastfeeding kar raha hai, to positioning aur attachment sudhaarne se unhe shaant hone mein madad mil sakti hai; iske liye aap breastfeeding group ya apne health visitor se madad le sakte hain [5]. Agar bachcha constant rota hai aur aap use chup kara nahi paate, ya uski rone ki awaaz aam jaisi nahi lagti, to yeh bimaari ka sanket ho sakta hai — agar use tez bukhaar hai ya doodh peene mein dilchaspi nahi hai to apne doctor se milen [7].

Turant madad len agar bachche ko daura (seizure) aata hai, honth ya skin neeli, grey, pale ya blotchy ho jaati hai, woh responsive nahi hai ya aaram se nahi jaagta, saans lene mein dikkat hai, bahut zyada ulti ho rahi hai, temperature bahut zyada ya bahut kam hai, aisi rash hai jo dabane par bhi nahi jaati, ya pichhle 8 ghante mein peshaab nahi kiya [7].

q: mere bete ko saans lene mein dikkat lag rahi hai

Saans lene mein dikkat kai cheezon se ho sakti hai — RSV, bronchiolitis, croup ya asthma jaisi bimariyan bhi isme shamil hain [2][3][5][6]. Bronchiolitis mein shuruaat zukaam jaisi hoti hai, phir khansi, tez saans, wheezing ya crackling awaaz, aur doodh peene mein dikkat ho sakti hai [5]. Abhi bachche ko seedha aur aaram se rakhein, aur saans lene mein madad ke liye kuch bhi muh mein na daalein [5]. Agar bachcha doodh ya khana kam le raha hai to thoda thoda, baar baar dein [5].

Turant madad lein agar bachche ki saans lene mein dikkat ho — grunting, pasliyan andar khinchti hon ya tez saans — saans mein rukawat aaye, hont ya chehra neela ya grey ho, ya bachcha bilkul dheela ho aur jagane par na jage [5]. q: my 2 year old has bad cough at night not sleeping
text:
A cough that is worse at night is common in whooping cough: after about a week of cold-like symptoms, children get coughing bouts that last for a few minutes and are worse at night, according to the NHS [3]. The cough may last for several weeks or months [3]. Coughing fits that get worse and happen more often, especially at night, can go on for up to 10 weeks or more, and recovery is slow, according to MedlinePlus [4].

Ask a pharmacist about cough syrup or cough medicine — some cough medicines should not be given to children under 12 years old — and these will not stop the cough but may help them cough less [1].

Ask for an urgent appointment or get help from your local emergency number if the cough is very bad or quickly gets worse, they feel very unwell, have chest pain, the side of their neck feels swollen and painful, they find it hard to breathe, or they are coughing up blood [1].

q: my 6 year old child is not eating anything from 2 days
text:
It's natural to worry when a child refuses to eat, but it's normal for children to refuse food sometimes, according to the NHS [6]. Don't worry about what your child eats in a day — it's more helpful to think about what they eat over a week [6]. If your child is active and gaining weight, and seems well, they're getting enough to eat [6]. As long as they eat some food from the 4 main food groups — fruit and vegetables; potatoes, bread, rice, pasta and other starchy carbohydrates; dairy or dairy alternatives; and beans, pulses, fish, eggs, meat and other proteins — you do not need to worry [6].

Give your child the same food as the rest of the family, without adding salt [3]. Give small portions and praise them for eating, even if they only eat a little [3]. If they reject the food, don't force them — take it away without saying anything and try again another time [3]. Don't give too many snacks between meals; 2 healthy snacks a day is plenty [3]. Keep offering a variety of foods, as it may take lots of attempts before your child accepts some foods [6].

q: my 6 month old baby has congested chest and making whistling noise
banner: 🚨 With these symptoms your child should be seen in the emergency department today, without waiting. | Reason: Breathing difficulty: fast breathing, wheezing, ribs pulling in
text:
A congested chest with a whistling noise when breathing can be bronchiolitis, which often starts like a cold and then brings a cough, faster breathing, trouble feeding and noisy breathing or wheezing, according to the NHS [2]. Symptoms are usually worst between days 3 and 5, and the cough usually gets better in 3 weeks [2].

Keep offering feeds often, in smaller amounts, because babies with this often feed less than usual [2][4]. If feeding is difficult, offer small sips or short, frequent feeds rather than one long feed [2].

Get help right away if there are pauses in your baby's breathing, if their skin, tongue or lips look blue or grey — on brown or black skin, check the palms, soles, lips, gums and inside the eyelids — or if they are floppy and will not wake up or stay awake [2]. Also get urgent help if a cold is getting worse, if they are feeding much less than normal, if they have had a dry nappy for 12 hours or more or show other signs of dehydration, if they feel hotter than usual or sweaty, if they are very tired or irritable, or if you are worried about them [2].

q: bukhar (उम्र: 6 महीने) (वज़न: 5 किलो)
text:
बुखार छोटे बच्चों में बहुत आम है और आमतौर पर 1 से 4 दिनों में तापमान सामान्य हो जाता है [1]। 38°C या उससे ज़्यादा तापमान बुखार माना जाता है [1]।

बच्चे को खूब तरल पदार्थ दें – अगर शिशु स्तनपान करता है तो सामान्य रूप से स्तनपान जारी रखें, निर्जलीकरण के संकेतों पर नज़र रखें, भूख लगे तो खाना दें, दिन-रात नियमित रूप से बच्चे की जाँच करें, और बच्चे को घर पर रखें [4]। अगर बच्चा परेशान या असहज लगे तो पैरासिटामोल या आइबुप्रोफेन दें – पैकेजिंग या पर्ची देखकर पुष्टि करें कि दवा बच्चे के लिए उपयुक्त है, या संदेह हो तो फार्मासिस्ट या डॉक्टर से बात करें [4]। बच्चे को कपड़ों या चादरों में ज़्यादा न लपेटें [2]। 16 साल से कम उम्र के बच्चों को एस्पिरिन न दें [2]। डॉक्टर या नर्स के कहने के बिना आइबुप्रोफेन और पैरासिटामोल बारी-बारी न दें [2]। 2 महीने से कम उम्र के बच्चे को पैरासिटामोल न दें [2]। 3 महीने से कम उम्र के, 5 किलो से कम वज़न वाले, चिकनपॉक्स वाले या निर्जलीकरण वाले बच्चे को आइबुप्रोफेन न दें [2]।

अगर बच्चा 3 से 6 महीने का है और तापमान 39°C या उससे ज़्यादा है, या आपको लगता है कि उसे बुखार है, तो तुरंत सलाह लें [2]। अगर बुखार के साथ दाने जैसे बीमारी के अन्य संकेत हों, बुखार 5 दिन या उससे ज़्यादा रहा हो, बच्चा खाना न चाहे या अपने सामान्य स्वभाव का न लगे और आप चिंतित हों, या निर्जलीकरण हो – जैसे कम गीले नैपी, धँसी आँखें, रोते समय आँसू न आना – तो भी तुरंत सलाह लें [2]।

ध्यान दें: WHO के विकास चार्ट के अनुसार 6 महीने के बच्चे के लिए 5 किग्रा बहुत कम वज़न है। अगर वज़न सही है तो जल्द ही डॉक्टर से बच्चे की बढ़त जँचवाएँ; अगर लिखने में गलती हुई है तो उसे ठीक करें, क्योंकि दवा की खुराक वज़न से तय होती है।

q: क्या बुखार उतारने के लिए बच्चे को नहला सकती हूँ? (उम्र: 6 महीने) (वज़न: 5 किलो)
text:
नहीं, बुखार उतारने के लिए बच्चे को नहलाना या स्पंज करना नहीं चाहिए — तेज़ तापमान संक्रमण के प्रति शरीर की स्वाभाविक और स्वस्थ प्रतिक्रिया है, ऐसा NHS कहता है [7]। बच्चे को ज़्यादा कपड़ों या रज़ाई में भी न लपेटें [7]।

बुखार उतारने के लिए गुनगुने पानी में कपड़ा भिगोकर पूरा शरीर पोंछ लें, सिर्फ माथा नहीं, और बच्चे का खाना-पीना चालू रखने की कोशिश करें, ऐसा भारत स्वास्थ्य कहता है [3]। बच्चे का तापमान डिजिटल थर्मामीटर से बगल में नापें; अगर बच्चे ने अभी नहाया है या कंबल में लपेटा गया है, तो तापमान कुछ देर के लिए ज़्यादा दिख सकता है — कुछ मिनट रुककर फिर नापें [1]।

अगर बच्चा 3 से 6 महीने का है और तापमान 39C या उससे ज़्यादा है, या आपको लगता है कि उसे तेज़ बुखार है, तो मदद लें [7]। इसके अलावा अगर बुखार के साथ दाने हों, बुखार 5 दिन या ज़्यादा से है, बच्चा खाना नहीं चाहता या अपने सामान्य स्वभाव का नहीं लगता और आपको चिंता है, या पानी की कमी हो — जैसे पेशाब कम आना, धँसी आँखें, रोते समय आँसू न आना — तो भी मदद लें [7]।

ध्यान दें: WHO के विकास चार्ट के अनुसार 6 महीने के बच्चे के लिए 5 किग्रा बहुत कम वज़न है। अगर वज़न सही है तो जल्द ही डॉक्टर से बच्चे की बढ़त जँचवाएँ; अगर लिखने में गलती हुई है तो उसे ठीक करें, क्योंकि दवा की खुराक वज़न से तय होती है।

q: 3 साल के बच्चे को सूखी खांसी और छाती से सीटी की आवाज आ रही है
banner: 🚨 इन लक्षणों के साथ बच्चे को आज ही इमरजेंसी में दिखाना चाहिए, देर न करें। | कारण: साँस की दिक्कत: तेज़ साँस, सीटी जैसी आवाज़, पसलियाँ दिखना
text:
सूखी खांसी और सांस लेते समय सीटी जैसी आवाज़ ब्रोंकियल (श्वसन मार्ग) में रुकावट से होने वाले लक्षण हैं, जो सांस की नली के संकुचन से बनते हैं और सल्ब्यूटामोल जैसी ब्रोंकोडाइलेटर दवाओं से ठीक हो सकते हैं, SEUP के अनुसार [2]। छोटे बच्चों में ऐसी सीटी की आवाज़ का सबसे आम कारण सांस की वायरल संक्रमण होती है [2]।

घर पर बच्चे को आराम दें और सांस लेने में तकलीफ़ बढ़ने पर तुरंत मदद लें। SEUP के अनुसार, सांस लेने में तकलीफ़ — पसलियाँ दिखाई देना, तेज़ सांस लेना, सांस लेते समय सीटी की आवाज़ — होने पर आपातकालीन विभाग जाना चाहिए [1]। MedlinePlus के अनुसार, तेज़ खांसी, सांस लेने में गंभीर तकलीफ़ और चेहरे, होंठों या नाखूनों का पीला या नीला पड़ना गंभीर दौरे के चेतावनी संकेत हैं, और ऐसे लक्षण हों तो तुरंत चिकित्सकीय सहायता लें [7]।

q: मेरे 5 साल के बच्चे के शरीर पर लाल दाने हो गए हैं और खुजली है
text:
बहुत खुजली वाले उभरे हुए दाने छोटे माइट्स के कारण हो सकते हैं जो त्वचा में घुस जाते हैं (स्केबीज़)। अक्सर उंगलियों के बीच एक सिरे पर बिंदु वाली उभरी हुई रेखाएँ दिखती हैं [4]। स्केबीज़ का इलाज आमतौर पर घर पर ही किया जा सकता है [4]।

5 साल या उससे बड़े बच्चे इलाज शुरू करते ही स्कूल जा सकते हैं, लेकिन पहले 24 घंटे दूसरों से नज़दीकी संपर्क से बचें [1]। इलाज माइट्स को जल्दी मार देता है, पर खुजली कुछ हफ़्ते तक चल सकती है [1]। स्केबीज़ नज़दीकी त्वचा संपर्क से फैलता है; पालतू जानवरों से नहीं होता [1]। यह किसी को भी हो सकता है, इसका सफ़ाई से कोई लेना-देना नहीं [1]। खुजाने से त्वचा में संक्रमण जैसे इम्पेटिगो हो सकता है, और एक्ज़िमा या सोरायसिस बिगड़ सकते हैं [1]।

डॉक्टर से मिलें अगर घर में किसी और को भी स्केबीज़ है, त्वचा में संक्रमण लगता है या कोई और त्वचा रोग जैसे एक्ज़िमा है, कोहनी, घुटनों, हाथों या पैरों पर पपड़ीदार परतदार दाने हैं, या फ़ार्मेसी का इलाज पूरा होने के 2 से 4 हफ़्ते बाद भी खुजली बनी हुई है [1]।

q: क्या एमएमआर वैक्सीन बच्चे के लिए सुरक्षित है
text: वैक्सीन्स काफी सुरक्षित हैं और इनके दुष्प्रभाव मामूली से लेकर गंभीर तक हो सकते हैं, जिनका मामूली उपचार से इलाज हो सकता है, विकासपीडिया के अनुसार [6]। दुष्प्रभाव होना इस बात का संकेत है कि वैक्सीन असर दिखा रही है [6]। कोई भी वैक्सीन शत-प्रतिशत प्रभावशाली नहीं होती [2]। टीके सुरक्षित, प्रभावी हैं और जान बचा सकते हैं, एनआईडायरेक्ट के अनुसार [4]। एमएमआर वैक्सीन सहित टीकाकरण का समय और आयु भारत के राष्ट्रीय टीकाकरण कार्यक्रम के अनुसार तय होती है [1]। अपने बच्चे के टीकाकरण के बारे में किसी भी सवाल के लिए अपने डॉक्टर से बात करें [3]।

q: 3 saal ke bacche ko raat ko bahut khansi aati hai
text:
Raat ki khansi 3 saal ke bachche mein aam hai: asthma ke lakshanon mein khansi khaas taur par raat ko ya subah jaldi hona shamil hai [5]. SEUP ke mutabik laringitis mein bhi bachche raat ko kaafi khansi karte hain aur theek se sote nahi [6].

Ghar par: agar bukhar ho to liquids dijiye aur aam antitérmicos (bukhar ki dawa) dijiye [6]. SEUP kehti hai ki bachche ko kuch din ghar par aaram karne dena achha hai [6]. MedlinePlus ke mutabik khansi-zukam ke liye bachche ko aaram, kaafi liquids, saaf humidifier ya thanda vaporizer, saline nasal drops, aur dard ya khansi ki OTC dawa di ja sakti hai — lekin bachchon ko aspirin bilkul nahi deni chahiye, aur koi bhi khansi-zukam ki dawa dene se pehle apne doctor se baat karein [4].

Turant madad lein agar: saans lene mein dikkat ya tez saans, dehydration, 4 din se zyada bukhar, 10 din se zyada lakshan bina sudhaar, ya bukhar/khansi jo behtar hokar wapas bigad jaye [4]. Asthma ke severe attack ke warning signs: tez khansi, saans lene mein gambhir dikkat, aur chehre, hothon ya naakhunon ka pale ya neela padna — aise lakshan hon to turant medical help lein [5].

q: mera 8 month ka baby bed se gir gaya aur ro raha hai
text:
Girne ke baad sar par chot lagne ko head injury kehte hain, jo aksar girne se hoti hai [1]. Iske aam lakshan hain sar dard, uljhan, thodi der ke liye yaadash chali jana, chakkar aana, ji michalna, ulti aur neend aana [1].

Ghar par dhyan rakhein ki upar bataye lakshan na aayein [6]. Agar sar dard ho, to SEUP ke mutabik ibuprofeno ya paracetamol di ja sakti hai, us matra mein jo aapke doctor ne batayi ho [6]. Bachcha so sakta hai, lekin zyada bhaari chot mein use har 4 ghante mein jagana theek rehta hai [6]. Khaane mein koi khaas badlav ki zarurat nahi, apni bhookh ke hisaab se pehle jaisa khilayein [6]. Zyadatar bachche jaldi theek ho jate hain, kuch mein kuch ghanton ya kuch din tak lakshan reh sakte hain [6].

Turant madad lein agar sar dard badhta jaye ya theek na ho, baar-baar ulti ho, bachcha bhramit ya confused lage, bahut chhoti umar mein chidchida ho ya jagane par mushkil se jaage, uska vyavhaar badal jaye, bolne ya chalne mein dikkat ho, ya naak ya kaan se khoon ya saaf paani aaye [2]. Urgent care bhi jayein agar bachcha 3 mahine se chhota ho, ya girne ki unchai ek meter se zyada thi [5].

q: 5 saal ke child ko body pe red rashes ho gaye hain
text:
5 saal ke bachche mein sharir par laal daane kai alag-alag kaaranon se ho sakte hain, aur MedlinePlus ke mutabik ye kisi bhi tarah ke skin irritation ya allergy ka lakshan ho sakte hain [2]. Kuch daane turant dikhte hain aur kuch kuch dinon mein ban jaate hain; zyadatar daane jaldi theek ho jaate hain, lekin kuch lambe samay tak rehte hain aur unka ilaaj chahiye hota hai [2]. Kai daane khujli wale, laal, dard bhare aur chubhne wale hote hain, aur kuch mein chhaale ya kachchi skin ke dhabbe bhi ban sakte hain [2].

Kyunki daane kai alag-alag cheezon se hote hain, isliye ilaaj se pehle ye pata karna zaroori hai ki kaunse prakar ke daane hain [2]. Agar daane gambhir hain, theek nahi ho rahe, ya saath mein doosre lakshan bhi hain, to apne doctor se milna chahiye [2]. Ilaaj mein moisturizer, lotion, snan, sujan kam karne wali cortisone cream, aur khujli kam karne wali antihistamine dawa shamil ho sakti hai [2].
sources: [2] MedlinePlus — "Rashes" (2025), p. 1 — https://medlineplus.gov/rashes.html

q: kya polio ki drop dena zaroori hai
text:
Polio ki drop dena zaroori hai. OMS ke mutabiq polio ki vaccine (antipoliomielítica inactivada) aksar difteria, tetanus, tosferina, Haemophilus influenzae aur hepatitis B ki vaccines ke saath mil kar di jaati hai [6]. CAV-AEP kehti hai ki jo bachay risk mein hain, unhein bhi apne schedule ki vaccines bina der ke deni chahiye [2].

Apne doctor se poochhein ki aapke bachay ko polio ki kaunsi dose, kab aur kitni baar deni hai — yeh aapke mulk ke vaccination schedule par depend karta hai. Vaccination ke liye doctor ke paas jaate waqt apne bachay ka vaccination card saath le jaayein, taaki pending doses ka pata chal sake [1].

Agar aapke bachay ko koi vaccine chhoot gayi hai ya aapko schedule samajh nahi aa raha, to apne doctor ya local health centre se baat karein.

q: my baby has diarrhea after we came back from a trip
text:
Diarrhoea is usually a symptom of an infection in the digestive tract, which can be caused by many different bacteria, viruses and parasites, and it is spread through contaminated food or drinking water, or from person to person because of poor hygiene, according to the WHO [6].

Treatment includes rehydration with oral rehydration salts — a mixture of clean water, salt and sugar — and zinc supplements, which reduce the length of a diarrhoea episode by 25% and are linked to a 30% reduction in stool volume [1]. Keep giving nutrient-rich foods, including breast milk, during the episode [1]. Do not use homemade solutions or commercial soft drinks to replace the losses from gastroenteritis, and do not give medicines for diarrhoea or vomiting without consulting your paediatrician, according to the SEUP [3].

See a health professional for persistent diarrhoea, blood in the stool, or signs of dehydration [1]. The SEUP says to seek help if the child is very thirsty, cries without tears, urinates little or has sunken eyes; is very irritable, drowsy or less responsive; has stools so watery, large and frequent that the child cannot drink as fast as they lose fluid; refuses to eat or drink; or has persistent or intense abdominal pain or stools with a lot of blood [3].

q: my child has been in the sun and now feels dizzy
text:
Heat exhaustion is what usually causes dizziness after time in the sun, and it does not usually need emergency medical help if you can cool the child down within 30 minutes, according to the NHS [1]. Dizziness is one of its symptoms, along with tiredness, headache, feeling sick or being sick, heavy sweating and pale clammy skin, cramps, a high temperature, thirst and irritability [1].

Move them to a cool place and take off unnecessary clothing like a jacket or socks. Give them plenty of water, or an isotonic sports drink or oral rehydration powder mixed with water. Cool their skin by spraying or sponging with cool water and fanning them; cold packs wrapped in a cloth under the armpits or on the neck work too. Stay with them until they are better — they should start to cool down and feel better within 30 minutes [7].

Get help now if they are still unwell after 30 minutes of resting in a cool place, being cooled and drinking fluids; have a very high temperature; hot skin that is not sweating and might look red; a fast heartbeat; fast breathing or shortness of breath; confusion and lack of coordination; a seizure or fit; or loss of consciousness [7].

Give an oral rehydration solution — a mixture of clean water, salt and sugar — and keep giving nutrient-rich foods, including breast milk, during the episode [2]. q: is MMR vaccine safe for my daughter
text: The MMR vaccine is safe, and research has shown there is no link between the MMR vaccine and autism, according to the NHS [4]. Like all medicines, it can cause side effects, but not everyone will get them [4]. Common side effects are usually mild and only last 2 to 3 days, and include a raised, blotchy rash, feeling unwell and a high temperature around 7 to 11 days after the vaccination, and swollen glands around the cheeks, neck and jaw and aching in the joints around 2 to 3 weeks after the vaccination [4]. More serious side effects, such as a severe allergic reaction (anaphylaxis), are rare, and the person who vaccinates your child will be trained to deal with allergic reactions and treat them immediately [4]. Protection starts within 2 weeks of having the vaccine, and after 2 doses around 99% of people will be protected against measles and rubella and around 88% against mumps [1]. The ages at which the vaccine is offered follow India's national schedule.

q: my 5 year old has stomach pain and constipation
text:
Stomach ache and constipation often go together: you may have a stomach ache and feel bloated or sick when you are constipated, according to the NHS [1]. Constipation is likely if your child has not had a poo at least 3 times in the last week, or is pooing less often than usual, if the poo is unusually large or small and dry, hard or lumpy, or if they strain or are in pain when they poo [1].

For a child over 6 months, the main things are to increase how much they drink, preferably water, to soften the poos, and to give more meals with fibre — wholegrain cereals and bread, fruit and vegetables. Do not replace fruit with juice, as juice has little fibre [3]. Most cases of childhood constipation (95%) are not caused by any illness, and it is not essential for a child to poo every day [3]. Do not give laxatives or enemas without asking your paediatrician [3].

See your paediatrician rather than going to the emergency department unless the constipation comes with: significant abdominal pain, if your child is very down and complaining a lot; blood in the poo; or vomiting many times and not keeping down solids or liquids [3].

Small, itchy raised spots like these are often heat rash, which is uncomfortable but usually harmless and usually gets better on its own after a few days, according to the NHS [3]. It can appear anywhere on the body and spread, but it cannot be passed on to other people [3].

Keep the skin cool so he does not sweat and irritate the rash: loose cotton clothing, lightweight bedding, cool baths or showers, and plenty of fluid to avoid dehydration [3]. If it is a bad rash, if it does not go away, or if there are other symptoms, see your doctor, according to MedlinePlus [4].

A severe cough and catarrh in a 4-year-old can be the early phase of whooping cough, which often starts like a cold with a runny nose, sneezing and a mild or occasional cough, according to the CDC [3]. q: my 3 year old has watery stool and weakness
text:
Watery stools with weakness in a 3-year-old is usually diarrhoea, which is loose or liquid stools passed three or more times a day, according to the WHO [3]. It is common and often lasts about one or two days, though it may last longer [4].

Treat it with oral rehydration salts (ORS) — a mixture of clean water, salt and sugar — and give zinc supplements, which shorten the episode by 25% and reduce stool volume by 30% [1]. Keep giving nutrient-rich foods, including breast milk, during the episode [1]. Children with diarrhoea should be given oral rehydration solutions to replace lost fluids and electrolytes, according to MedlinePlus [6].

Contact a health professional for persistent diarrhoea, blood in the stool, or signs of dehydration [1]. For a child, warning signs include a change in mental state such as irritability or lack of energy, diarrhoea lasting more than a day, high fever, frequent loose stools, vomiting often, severe belly or rectal pain, signs of dehydration such as thirst, dry mouth, urinating less than usual or no wet nappies for 3 hours or more, and no tears when crying, or black tarry stools or stools with blood or pus [2].

q: my baby fell from the bed and seems normal now

A knock on the head is the medical term for a blow to the head, usually from a fall, an accident or during sport, and the most common symptoms are headache, confusion, brief memory loss, dizziness, nausea, vomiting and drowsiness, according to the SEUP [1]. Most head injuries are mild and not dangerous, and tests are usually not needed; it is important to watch the child for the first 24 hours after the blow to spot serious symptoms [2].

For the next 24 to 48 hours, depending on how hard the blow was, keep them at physical and mental rest — no sport, no tablets, video games or smartphones — and then return to normal activities gradually [5]. Watch at home for a severe or worsening headache that does not improve with the usual paracetamol or ibuprofen, repeated vomiting, disorientation or confusion, and in very small children irritability or being hard to wake; also changes in usual behaviour, difficulty speaking or walking, and blood or clear fluid from the nose or ears [5].

Go to the emergency department if any of those symptoms appear, or if their behaviour or mood worries you, and also if the child is under three months old or the fall was from more than one metre, according to the SEUP [4]. MedlinePlus adds: get help immediately for a headache that worsens or does not improve, repeated vomiting or nausea, seizures, being unable to get up, dilated pupils in one or both eyes, difficulty speaking, weakness or numbness in the arms or legs, lack of coordination, or growing confusion, restlessness or agitation [3].

q: my 6 month old has started eating food, what should I give first
text:
At around 6 months, how much your baby eats matters less than getting them used to the idea of eating — they still get most of their energy and nutrients from breast milk or first infant formula [1]. The World Health Organization recommends introducing complementary foods at 6 months (180 days) while continuing to breastfeed [4].

Offer a variety of foods alongside breast or formula milk, and gradually increase the amount and variety until they can eat the same foods as the family, in smaller portions [1]. Include iron-containing foods such as meat, fish, fortified breakfast cereals, dark green vegetables, beans and lentils, plus fruit and vegetables, starchy foods like potatoes, bread, rice and pasta, and pasteurised full-fat dairy such as plain yoghurt and cheese [2]. Babies do not need salt or sugar added to their food or cooking water [2]. As they become more confident, offer more mashed, lumpy and finger foods; finger foods at each meal help them feed themselves and learn to chew and swallow [2]. There is no right or wrong way between finger foods and spoon-feeding — the important thing is a wide variety of food [3]. If your baby was born prematurely, ask your health visitor or doctor when to start [1].

q: how do I know if my child is dehydrated from diarrhoea
text:
Signs of dehydration include being very thirsty, crying without tears, passing little urine, or sunken eyes, according to the SEUP [2]. Marked irritability, drowsiness or reduced responsiveness also point to it [2]. So do stools so watery, heavy and frequent that the child cannot drink as fast as they lose fluid, refusing to eat or drink, and persistent or intense tummy pain or stools with a lot of blood [2]. The younger the child, the greater the danger of dehydration [2].

Keep giving oral rehydration solution, which comes already prepared — homemade solutions and commercial soft drinks should not be used to replace losses from gastroenteritis [2]. Do not give medicines for diarrhoea or vomiting without consulting your paediatrician [2]. The WHO also lists zinc supplements, which shorten a diarrhoea episode by 25% and are linked to a 30% reduction in stool volume, and continued nutrient-rich foods including breast milk [1][3]. Consult a health professional, particularly for persistent diarrhoea, blood in the stool, or signs of dehydration [1][3].

Most head injuries are not serious, and most children recover quickly, according to the NHS [2]. A knock to the head is usually from a fall, an accident or sport, and the usual symptoms are headache, confusion, brief memory loss, dizziness, nausea, vomiting and drowsiness [1].

q: my 4 year old has cough with phlegm at night
text:
A cough with phlegm can be a symptom of pneumonia, which can range from mild to severe, according to MedlinePlus [1]. A cough that is worse at night can also be a sign of whooping cough, which often starts like a cold and then brings coughing bouts that last for a few minutes and are worse at night, according to the NHS [3].

For a 4 year old with a cough, the CDC advises rest, plenty of fluids, a clean humidifier or cool mist vaporizer, saline nasal spray or drops, and breathing in steam from a bowl of hot water or a running shower [5]. Honey can be used to relieve cough in children at least 1 year old [5]. Over-the-counter cough and cold medicines are not recommended for children younger than 6 years old [5].

Ask for an urgent appointment with your doctor if your child has had a cough for up to 3 weeks, is coughing up yellow or green mucus, has chest pain that comes and goes or happens when breathing or coughing, or is feeling short of breath [2]. Get emergency help if your child is struggling to breathe, has pale, blue or blotchy skin, lips or tongue, is coughing up blood, or suddenly feels confused [2].

On steam, guidelines differ. The CDC suggests sitting with a young child in a bathroom with steam from a running shower to ease a cough. The NHS advises against it: with croup, do not put your child in a steamy room or get them to inhale steam, and do not let children breathe in steam from a bowl of hot water, because of the risk of scalding.

text:
A chest infection is an infection of the lungs or large airways, and it often follows a cold or flu, according to the NHS [2]. The main symptoms are a chesty cough, sometimes with green or yellow mucus, wheezing and shortness of breath, chest pain or discomfort, a high temperature, headache, aching muscles and tiredness [2]. These symptoms can be unpleasant, but they usually get better on their own in about 7 to 10 days, and the cough and mucus can last up to 3 weeks [2].

For the flu itself, the World Health Organization says treatment should aim to relieve symptoms: rest and drink plenty of liquids [5]. Most people recover on their own within a week [5]. Over-the-counter cough and flu medicine should not be given to children younger than 6 years old unless a health care provider advises it [4].

Seek medical care if your child has severe symptoms, according to the WHO [3].

q: what solids to give first to 6 month baby
text:
Introducing solid foods should start when your baby is around 6 months old, according to the NHS [3]. At the beginning, how much your baby eats matters less than getting them used to the idea of eating — they'll still get most of their energy and nutrients from breast milk or first infant formula [3].

You can offer purées, mashed foods, cereals and baby rice added to milk, or finger foods they pick up themselves; there's no right or wrong way, and a mix of both is fine [1][2]. Giving a variety of foods alongside breast or formula milk from around 6 months helps set your child up for healthier eating, and you can gradually increase the amount and variety until they eat the same foods as the family in smaller portions [3]. Continue breastfeeding or first infant formula until at least 1 year [4]. Offer sips of water with meals from a cup [5]. Sit your baby upright in a high chair with a safety harness, and never leave them unattended on raised surfaces [5].

q: my 4 year old child has small red bumps on face and neck
text: Small red bumps on the face and neck can be the rash of roseola, which is a very common infection that mainly affects babies and toddlers, according to the NHS. With roseola, a child first has a sudden high temperature, cold-like symptoms such as a sore throat, runny nose and cough, loss of appetite, and swollen eyelids and glands in the neck; these last 3 to 5 days before the rash appears [2]. The rash is made up of pinkish-red spots, patches or bumps, starts on the chest, tummy and back before spreading to the face, neck and arms, is not usually itchy or uncomfortable, and normally fades and disappears within 2 days [2]. You can normally look after your child at home and they should recover within a week [2].

q: my 1 year old baby body is very hot since morning
text:
A high temperature in a baby is usually considered to be 38C or above, and you can usually look after your baby at home when they have one, according to the NHS [2][6]. Your baby may feel hotter than usual to touch on their back or chest, feel sweaty or clammy, or have flushed cheeks [2]. Check their temperature with a thermometer if you can — it helps you work out whether you need to get medical advice [2].

Give them plenty of drinks to avoid dehydration, and if you're breastfeeding, offer plenty of feeds [6].

Ask for an urgent appointment with your doctor if your child has other signs of illness, such as a rash, as well as a high temperature [6]. Get help immediately if a baby or young child has a high temperature and a rash that does not fade when you roll a glass over it [6].

q: my baby has vomiting and loose motion since morning
text:
Vomiting and loose stools together are most often caused by a stomach bug, according to the NHS [1]. It usually settles on its own: diarrhoea usually stops within 5 to 7 days and vomiting usually stops in 1 or 2 days [6].

Keep fluids going in. Offer an oral rehydration solution, in small amounts and often, and keep breastfeeding normally, even more often if your baby wants it [5]. Do not water down formula — use it at its usual strength [6]. Avoid fruit juice, fizzy drinks, sweets and sports drinks, as these can make diarrhoea worse [5][6]. Do not give medicine to stop diarrhoea to a child under 12 [6].

Get help now if your baby is under 3 months and has vomited two or more feeds; vomits a lot or cannot keep down solids or liquids; the vomit is green, bloody or looks like coffee grounds; is drowsy, floppy, very thirsty, has sunken eyes, cries without tears or is passing little urine; or has severe tummy pain or a headache [2]. Also get help if there is any change in your baby's alertness or energy, diarrhoea lasting more than a day, any fever in an infant, frequent loose stools, vomiting often, severe tummy pain, signs of dehydration such as thirst, dry mouth, fewer wet nappies or no wet nappy for 3 hours or more, or stools that are black and tarry or contain blood [4].

text:
Fast breathing with a cough can be a sign of bronchiolitis, which often starts like an ordinary cold with cough and mucus, and after 2–4 days the child may breathe faster, be irritable and find feeding harder, according to the SEUP [3]. In children under 5 with cough or difficulty breathing, fast breathing or chest indrawing points to pneumonia, according to the WHO [7].

Keep the child comfortable and let them rest; sleeping in a semi-upright position is advised for a child with chest indrawing or difficulty breathing [6]. Offer fluids and feeds often, in small amounts, and watch how well they take them [6].

Get urgent help if the child's general state worsens — floppy, sleepy or very irritable — or if breathing difficulty appears, according to the SEUP [2]. Also get help if they have a bad colour, chest or side pain when breathing, persistently refuse food and fluids, or do not tolerate the prescribed treatment [5].

Yes, paracetamol can help if your child is distressed or uncomfortable because they have a high temperature, according to the NHS [3]. It is a common painkiller for children that helps relieve pain and high temperature [4].

q: can I give ORS to my 1 year old after diarrhea
text: Yes, you can give oral rehydration salts to a 1-year-old after diarrhoea. Rehydration with ORS solution is a key treatment for diarrhoea, according to the WHO [1]. ORS is a mixture of clean water, salt and sugar that is absorbed in the small intestine and replaces the water and electrolytes lost in the faeces [1]. Zinc supplements are also a key treatment: they reduce the duration of a diarrhoea episode by 25% and are associated with a 30% reduction in stool volume [1]. A 10–14 day supplemental treatment course of dispersible zinc tablets shortens diarrhoea duration and improves outcomes [6]. Keep giving nutrient-rich foods, including breast milk, during the episode [1]. Do not use homemade solutions or commercial soft drinks to replace the losses from gastroenteritis, and do not give medicines for diarrhoea or vomiting without consulting your paediatrician, according to the SEUP [3]. Consult a health professional for persistent diarrhoea, blood in the stool, or signs of dehydration [1].

q: mi hijo tiene conjuntivitis y se le pegan los ojos al despertarse
text:
La conjuntivitis es el nombre médico de la "vista rosa": es una inflamación de la capa externa del ojo y del interior del párpado, y puede causar hinchazón, picor, escozor, secreción y enrojecimiento, según MedlinePlus [4]. En la mayoría de los casos se cura sin atención médica, aunque la conjuntivitis bacteriana necesita tratamiento con gotas o pomada antibiótica [4].

No hace falta que el niño se quede en casa ni falte al colegio, a menos que se encuentre muy mal, según el NHS [3].

Conviene consultar al médico si el niño es un bebé con los ojos rojos y pegajosos —con cita urgente si tiene menos de 30 días—, si lleva lentillas y además tiene granitos en los párpados, o si los síntomas no se han resuelto en 7 días [3]. Hay que pedir cita urgente o ayuda urgente si hay dolor en los ojos, sensibilidad a la luz, cambios en la visión como líneas onduladas o destellos, ojos muy rojos (uno o los dos), o un bebé de menos de 30 días con los ojos rojos y pegajosos, porque pueden ser signos de un problema ocular más grave [3].

text:
Si el niño tiene menos de 3 meses, la fiebre necesita que lo vea un médico el mismo día.

La meningitis puede agravarse muy rápido, según MedlinePlus, y la fiebre súbita con rigidez en el cuello es uno de los signos por los que hay que buscar atención médica de inmediato [7]. Mientras consiguen esa atención, mantén al niño acompañado y no lo dejes solo. La meningitis es la inflamación del tejido delgado que rodea el cerebro y la médula espinal, y los exámenes para diagnosticarla incluyen análisis de sangre, pruebas de imágenes y una punción espinal para examinar el líquido cefalorraquídeo [7]. El tratamiento temprano puede ayudar a prevenir problemas graves, incluyendo la muerte [7]. Los antibióticos pueden tratar la meningitis bacteriana y las medicinas antivirales pueden ayudar con algunos tipos de meningitis virales [7].

text:
Un golpe en la cabeza es un traumatismo craneal, y la mayoría de los traumatismos craneales son leves y no representan un peligro, según la SEUP [2]. Los síntomas más habituales son dolor de cabeza, confusión, pérdida de memoria transitoria, sensación de mareo, náuseas, vómitos y somnolencia [1].

Mientras la ven, mantén a tu hija en reposo físico y mental entre 24 y 48 horas, sin actividades deportivas ni dispositivos electrónicos, y después vuelve poco a poco a su rutina habitual [6]. Conviene vigilarla durante las primeras 24 horas tras el golpe [2].

Debe consultarse en urgencias si presenta alguno de esos síntomas, o si tiene un comportamiento o actitud que te preocupe, según la SEUP [3]. También se recomienda acudir si el menor tiene menos de tres meses o si la caída fue desde una altura superior a un metro [3]. Busca ayuda de inmediato si hay dolor de cabeza que empeora o no mejora, vómitos o náuseas reiteradas, convulsiones, incapacidad para levantarse, pupilas dilatadas en uno o ambos ojos, dificultad para hablar, debilidad o entumecimiento de brazos o piernas, falta de coordinación, o confusión, inquietud o agitación crecientes, según MedlinePlus [4].

q: mi hija de 13 años tiene reglas muy abundantes
text:
Puede ser normal tener reglas abundantes, según el NHS [1]. Se consideran abundantes si necesitas cambiar la compresa o el tampón cada 1 o 2 horas, si usas dos productos a la vez, si duran más de 7 días, si expulsas coágulos mayores de unos 2,5 cm, si manchas la ropa o la cama, si tiene que evitar actividades diarias o si se siente cansada o le falta el aire [1]. A veces se deben a afecciones del útero o los ovarios, a problemas que hacen sangrar más fácilmente o a algunos medicamentos [5].

El tratamiento puede ayudar cuando las reglas afectan a la vida diaria [1]. Consulta a tu médico si las reglas abundantes le afectan a su vida, si lleva tiempo con ellas, si tiene dolor intenso durante la regla, si sangra entre reglas o después de relaciones sexuales, o si además tiene dolor al orinar, al hacer de vientre o al mantener relaciones [5].

q: mi hija se desmayo jugando al futbol pero ahora esta bien
banner: 🚨 Con estos síntomas hay que acudir a urgencias hoy, sin esperar. | Motivo: Desmayo haciendo ejercicio, o con palpitaciones o dolor en el pecho: que lo vean en urgencias hoy
text:
Un desmayo o síncope es una pérdida de conocimiento brusca y corta, según la SEUP [1]. Suele ocurrir cuando no llega suficiente sangre u oxígeno al cerebro, y el calor extremo, el dolor, el miedo o el esfuerzo pueden favorecerlo [1]. Antes de perder el conocimiento puede haber náuseas, visión borrosa, dolor abdominal, sudoración o zumbidos, señales que ayudan a reconocer lo que va a pasar y a evitar nuevos desmayos [2].

Si vuelve a sentirse mal, que se siente o se tumbe de inmediato, y que respire lenta y profundamente [5]. Si pierde el conocimiento, túmbala con las piernas elevadas y la cabeza de lado para que respire mejor [5]. Cuando el malestar desaparezca, que se incorpore despacio: primero sentada y, tras unos minutos, de pie [5]. Tras un reposo suelen recuperarse en un par de minutos [5]. Conviene que beba más líquidos, sobre todo al hacer ejercicio [4].

Consulta en urgencias si tarda más de 3-5 minutos en recuperar el conocimiento —entonces colócala de lado y llama a emergencias—, si el desmayo ocurre haciendo ejercicio o esfuerzo, o si se acompaña de palpitaciones, dolor en el pecho, sacudidas de brazos y piernas o pérdida involuntaria de orina [3].

banner: 🚨 Con estos síntomas hay que acudir a urgencias hoy, sin esperar. | Motivo: Vomita TODO lo que toma y no retiene nada: es signo de peligro, hay que verlo hoy
text: Que el bebé vomite y no retenga ni sorbos pequeños es un signo de peligro: la SEUP indica consultar de nuevo en urgencias si el niño vomita mucho, no tolera sólidos ni líquidos, o vomita aunque no tome nada [4]. Mientras consiguen atención, ofrézcale solución de rehidratación oral ya preparada, en cantidades pequeñas y frecuentes, sin usar soluciones caseras ni refrescos comerciales [5]. Mantenga la lactancia materna normal, e incluso más a menudo si el bebé la pide [4]. No le dé medicamentos para la diarrea o los vómitos sin consultar con su pediatra [5]. q: cuando se puede empezar con la fruta y la verdura
text: La fruta y la verdura se pueden empezar a ofrecer en torno a los 6 meses, cuando la leche ya no cubre por sí sola las necesidades del bebé y hacen falta alimentos complementarios [2]. Según la AEP, se aconseja introducir progresivamente toda la variedad de frutas y verduras disponible, en cualquiera de las comidas diarias, variando también la forma de presentación (triturada, chafada, en pequeños trozos) [1]. No hay unas frutas mejores que otras para comenzar; la decisión depende de los gustos de la familia [1]. Conviene ofrecer los alimentos de uno en uno, con intervalos de unos días, para observar la tolerancia y la aceptación, y no añadirles sal, azúcar ni edulcorantes [4]. Durante el primer año, evita las verduras de hoja verde con alto contenido en nitratos, como la acelga, la espinaca o la borraja, por el riesgo de metahemoglobinemia [1]. Es mejor la fruta entera que los zumos, que no aportan beneficio nutricional frente a ella y aumentan el riesgo de caries [1].

q: mi hija de 5 años tiene granitos rojos por la tripa que le pican mucho
text:
Los granitos rojos que pican mucho pueden deberse a una reacción alérgica (urticaria), según el NHS, y la urticaria normalmente se puede tratar en casa [5]. También pueden ser sudamina: pequeños granitos en relieve con picor o escozor, y lo principal es mantener la piel fresca para no sudar e irritar el sarpullido [6].

Para calmar el picor, aplica algo frío, como un paño húmedo o una bolsa de hielo envuelta en un paño, hasta 20 minutos; da golpecitos o palmaditas en el sarpullido en vez de rascarlo, y no uses geles ni cremas perfumadas [6]. Usa ropa de algodón holgada, ropa de cama ligera y baños o duchas frescas, y que beba abundante líquido para evitar la deshidratación [6].

Llama a tu número local de emergencias si hay hinchazón alrededor de la boca o le cuesta respirar [5].

q: mi hijo es asmatico y se le hunden las costillas al respirar
banner: 🚨 Llama ahora al 112 o acude a urgencias. | Motivo: Dificultad para respirar grave (se marcan las costillas, respira muy rápido, pausas en la respiración, color azulado)
text: Que se le hundan las costillas al respirar (tiraje) es uno de los síntomas de una crisis asmática, según la SEUP [4]. En una crisis asmática, hay que iniciar tratamiento con salbutamol [3], administrando de 2 a 4 pulsaciones con una cámara espaciadora (y mascarilla facial en niños pequeños), de una en una, y repetir esa dosis a los 10-15 minutos [6]. Los inhaladores deben administrarse siempre con cámara, nunca directamente en la boca [3]. Mantén al niño en reposo, evita el ejercicio y los ambientes con humo o contaminación [6], y si toma tratamiento de mantenimiento, debe seguir con él durante la crisis [6]. Si la crisis no cede tras el tratamiento en casa, o si queda alguna duda, hay que acudir lo antes posible a un centro sanitario, sin olvidar la cámara espaciadora [6].

q: cuantas pufs de ventolin le doy
text:
De 2 a 4 pulsaciones de salbutamol (Ventolin), aplicadas de una en una con una cámara espaciadora y mascarilla facial en los niños pequeños, según la SEUP [5]. Repite esa dosis a los 10-15 minutos [5]. Los inhaladores deben administrarse siempre con cámara, nunca directamente en la boca [3].

Acude lo antes posible a un centro sanitario si la crisis no cede tras el tratamiento en casa o si te queda alguna duda, sin olvidar la cámara espaciadora [5]. También si está muy agitado o somnoliento, si se pone morado o pálido, si la dificultad respiratoria empeora (respira cada vez más deprisa, se le marcan las costillas, mueve mucho el abdomen o se le hunde el pecho) o si necesita inhalaciones cada dos horas o menos [3].

Comprueba siempre la concentración del envase. Si tiene menos de 3 meses, consulta antes de dar nada.

q: y si no le baja la fiebre le puedo dar dalsy
text: Sí, se puede cambiar de antitérmico si la fiebre no baja y el malestar no mejora. Según la SEUP, el paracetamol y el ibuprofeno tienen una eficacia similar y se pueden dar a la dosis recomendada por su pediatra cada 6-8 horas [1]. La AEPap añade que, si damos un antitérmico y a las 3-4 horas la temperatura sigue alta y el malestar no mejora, es razonable intercambiarlos: si empezamos con paracetamol y no mejora, la próxima vez se puede dar ibuprofeno en vez de paracetamol [6]. No se recomienda alternarlos de forma sistemática cada 3-4 horas, salvo que el niño presente malestar antes de las 6 horas o alguna enfermedad previa que lo justifique [1]. Conviene asegurarse de que esté bien hidratado y no forzarlo a comer [1]. Consulta si está decaído, poco reactivo o muy irritable, si le cuesta respirar, si tiene manchas en la piel que no desaparecen al presionarlas, si no tolera sólidos ni líquidos por boca, o si es menor de 2 meses o inmunodeprimido [7].

q: mi bebe lleva todo el dia sin hacer pis
banner: 🚨 Con estos síntomas hay que acudir a urgencias hoy, sin esperar. | Motivo: Signos de deshidratación: ojos hundidos, orina poco, boca seca, vómitos persistentes o diarrea abundante >24 h
text:
Según la SEUP, un bebé puede estar hasta 24 horas sin hacer pis después de la primera micción; pasado ese tiempo, debe mojar los pañales con frecuencia, con orina clara e inodora, sobre todo si toma solo leche materna [6].

Ofrécele líquidos en pequeñas cantidades y a menudo. Si tiene mucha sed, llora sin lágrimas, orina poco o tiene los ojos hundidos, es señal de que hay que consultar [1]. Dale solución de rehidratación oral ya preparada, no soluciones caseras ni refrescos [1]. Si toma pecho, mantén la lactancia normal, incluso más a menudo si lo pide [8]. No le des medicamentos para la diarrea o los vómitos sin consultar con su pediatra [1].

Consulta de nuevo en urgencias si vomita mucho, no tolera sólidos ni líquidos, o vomita aunque no tome nada; si los vómitos son verdosos, con sangre o parecen posos de café [8]. También si está muy irritable, somnoliento o responde menos [1].

q: mi hijo de 2 años tiene 39.5 de fiebre y las manos muy frias
banner: 🚨 Con estos síntomas hay que acudir a urgencias hoy, sin esperar. | Motivo: Manos y pies fríos en un niño con fiebre: puede ser mala circulación, hay que verlo
text:
Lo primero, haz lo que dice el aviso de arriba.

La fiebre es la respuesta natural del cuerpo para combatir una infección, según MedlinePlus [2]. Con fiebre, conviene tratar el malestar con antitérmicos, mantener una buena hidratación, no sobreabrigar al niño y tenerlo en una habitación ventilada y templada, según la SEUP [3]. Ofrécele líquidos a menudo, en sorbos pequeños y frecuentes, para prevenir la deshidratación [2]. No lo desvistas ni le des baños de esponja para bajarle la temperatura, y no lo tapes con demasiada ropa ni mantas, según el NHS [1]. No le des aspirina a un niño menor de 16 años [1]. No alternes ibuprofeno y paracetamol salvo que un profesional sanitario te lo indique [1]. No le des ibuprofeno si tiene menos de 3 meses, pesa menos de 5 kg, tiene varicela o está deshidratado [1]. La fiebre, y que continúe después de un antitérmico, no implican gravedad por sí mismas [3].

q: mi hijo tiene diarrea pero quiere comer normal
text:
La gastroenteritis suele mejorar por sí sola, con reposo y abundantes líquidos y electrolitos, según MedlinePlus [5]. Lo más importante es evitar la deshidratación por las pérdidas de líquido de las deposiciones y los vómitos: las soluciones de rehidratación oral llevan agua, azúcar y sales en una proporción precisa para compensar esas pérdidas [3]. Ofrécele la cantidad que te hayan indicado después de cada deposición líquida o cada vómito, en dosis pequeñas y tomas frecuentes para que las tolere bien [3]. No uses soluciones caseras ni refrescos comerciales, y no le des medicamentos para la diarrea o los vómitos sin consultar con su pediatra [2].

Consulta lo antes posible con un profesional de la salud si el niño tiene irritabilidad marcada, somnolencia o disminución de la capacidad de respuesta; si las deposiciones son muy líquidas, abundantes y frecuentes y no es capaz de beber al mismo ritmo que pierde; si rechaza comer o beber; o si tiene dolor abdominal persistente o intenso o deposiciones con mucha sangre [2].
